about: Stage 1.5 of the Job queue (trains the service builds, checks and lands) as request/response cases. research.jobs.trains runs them (tools/research/tests/test_jobs_vectors.py); the site's TypeScript runs the same file. Everything in vectors.json's `about` holds here too, and each case also starts from `setup.github` in a fake GitHub and an empty fake store. The fake GitHub: `commits` by id, each with `parents` and `files` (the paths it sets against its first parent; null deletes one); a commit's tree is its first-parent chain's files applied in order. `merge(ref, head)` (the Merges API): 204 when head is already an ancestor of the ref's tip; 409 when a path changed on both sides since their merge base has different contents; else 201 and a new commit named `{tip}+{head}` with parents [tip, head], and the ref moves to it. `update_ref(ref, sha)` with force false: 422 unless the old tip is an ancestor of sha; on success every open PR based on that ref whose head is now an ancestor becomes `merged`. The fake store holds `attempts` by run id and `manifests` by art id (a result's: its `kind` and `meta`). The gate reads main's tools/verity/check/tool.py by parsing it, never by running it or by the first match of a pattern: its one module-level `CHECK = Tool(...)`, a call with keyword arguments only, whose `produces` (a list of strings; missing: no kind passes) and `merge_requires` (an object of lists of strings; missing: no step is required) are each read as a literal; anything else lands nothing. Further step forms: `store` adds attempts and manifests (replacing one of the same id, which the real store never does, to keep the cases short); `github_push` puts someone else's commit on a ref (moving it without the fast-forward rule); `github_label` adds a label to a PR; `reconcile: true` runs the reconcile cron, whose `expect.moved` lists the train ids it moved; `expect_github` compares refs (null: the ref must be absent), PRs (a subset of each), the comments posted, in order, and `trees`: files at a commit (a subset). Lean records: when a merge step's two sides both changed a `lean-audit.json` whose contents differ, the service merges the three records (merge base, train, PR) with tools/lean/merge.py's `merge()` and writes the result with audit.py's `text()`. The result goes onto the train as a commit named `{tip}.rec` and onto the PR's head as `{head}.rec`. When `merge()` refuses, only `{head}.rec` is written, with the train's record, and the package (the record's directory) is regenerated: a `lean-regen` job on the tip, whose run's `records/{package}/lean-audit.json` (from its run record: `outputs.run_record`, then that manifest's `payload.files`, then `objects`) becomes the commit `{tip}.regen` before the merge check. `store` also takes `objects`.

files.tools/verity/check/tool.py:
"""Store declaration for the repository's check (research.store README §6.1; `tools/verity/check/check.py`).

    research run --tool check --project verity --cwd source -- uv run --locked --extra torch-cpu python tools/verity/check/check.py

No key params and no closure: the attempt's source (a clean commit) is the whole input, and `research merge` reads the attempt by
that commit.  A merge that changes verity/ml/flock/, other than a README.md or PROTOCOL.md (which nothing the agreement runs
reads), needs an attempt whose `lean-agreement` step passed (`merge_requires`; the step runs when the run has the pinned
upstream build, which `check.py --record` sends then).  `research run --on` refuses a machine that fails `preflight.py` (the pod
setup, the Lean dependencies, a store read, AVX-512 when needed, free disk) before the run is claimed.  Nothing here imports
anything but `research.store.tool`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from research.store.tool import Tool

CHECK = Tool(name="check", version="1", command=["uv", "run", "--locked", "--extra", "torch-cpu", "python", "tools/verity/check/check.py"],
             produces=["check/v1"],
             merge_requires={"lean-agreement": ["verity/ml/flock/", "!README.md", "!PROTOCOL.md"]},
             preflight=["tools/verity/check/preflight.py"])
